question: Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
grading: Reference-free (no fixed answer), graded for recency and support. Expect: announced 2026-09-29; reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of the workforce, primarily in Product and Technology, plus select leased office space reductions; estimated charges USD 65M-80M (about USD 55M-70M in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10M in Q4 FY2027); fiscal 2027 Q3 and full-year guidance reiterated except GAAP operating margin. Snapshot as of 2026-10-03.
answer: On September 29, 2026 Workday disclosed in an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 2.05) that certain functions announced reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its workforce, primarily within the Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions, while continuing to hire in strategic areas. It estimates charges of about USD 65-80 million, of which about USD 55-70 million in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10 million in Q4 FY2027 (roughly USD 40-55 million future cash for severance and benefits, about USD 10 million non-cash stock-based compensation and about USD 15 million non-cash lease impairment). Workday reiterated its Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance from August 27 except GAAP operating margin (now about 20-21 points below non-GAAP in Q3 and about 19 points below for the full year). [T16-E1, T16-E2] Separately, on October 1, 2026 Workday entered into a new USD 1.5 billion revolving credit agreement replacing its USD 1.0 billion 2022 facility; this is not part of the restructuring. [T16-E3]

output.answer:
Yes — Workday has announced several rounds of restructuring. The most recent is from late September 2026:

## Most recent: September 29, 2026 (Product & Technology)
- **Scope:** ~2.5% of workforce, roughly 500–525 employees, concentrated in the **Product and Technology** organization, plus some leased-office reductions. Stated rationale: "better align team structures with Workday's strategic growth priorities." The company says it will keep hiring in key strategic areas/locations during fiscal 2027.
- **Expected costs:** **$65 million–$80 million** total charges — about **$55M–$70M in fiscal Q3 2027** and ~$10M in Q4. That includes ~$40M–$55M in cash severance/benefits and stock-based compensation, plus a ~$15M office-lease write-down.
- **Margin impact:** GAAP operating margin for fiscal Q3 2027 is now expected to trail non-GAAP by 20–21 points. All other guidance was reaffirmed; the cuts should be largely complete by Q1 of fiscal 2028.
- Note: this came shortly after reports of a buyout bid taking shape, and followed a CEO change (Carl Eschenbach departed in February 2026, replaced by co-founder Aneel Bhusri).
- Sources: [Workday 8-K via StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/WDAY/8-k-workday-inc-reports-material-event-e5a30bf1a264.html), [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/workday-conducting-layoffs-software-product-tech-team-2026-9), [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/workday-layoffs-tech-team-ai-shift)

## Earlier round: February 2026 (Global Customer Operations)
- **Scope:** ~400 positions (~2% of workforce), primarily non-revenue-generating roles in the global customer service team, as part of "fiscal 2027" prioritization.
- **Expected costs:** approximately **$135 million** in restructuring and impairment charges (including an ~$80M office-space impairment), recognized largely in fiscal Q4 2026 (reported Feb. 24, 2026). GAAP operating margins guided 24–25 points lower for the quarter and 22–23 points lower for the full year. Completion targeted for late April 2026.
- Sources: [TechRepublic](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-workday-cuts-400-jobs), [HR Executive](https://hrexecutive.com/workday-files-more-job-cuts-customer-ops-teams-hit), [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/workday-layoffs-amid-software-stock-sell-off-2026-2)

## Original round: February 2025 ("Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan")
- **Scope:** workforce reduced by ~**7.5%** (~1,750 jobs), plus exiting certain owned office space, framed around prioritizing AI investment.
- **Costs:** During the nine months ended October 31, 2025, Workday recorded **$133 million** for employee transition, severance, benefits, and share-based compensation, plus **$39 million** for office-space impairment.
- Source: [Workday Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2025/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results-11-25-2025/default.aspx); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/21/ai-job-cuts-amazon-microsoft-and-more-cite-ai-for-2025-layoffs.html)

**Bottom line:** Workday has now executed three restructuring rounds since early 2025, with the two most recent (Feb and Sept 2026) each around 2–2.5% of headcount and carrying roughly $135M and $65–80M in charges respectively — a pattern the press has characterized as ongoing rotation toward AI/product priorities rather than a retreat, since headcount still grew ~3% in fiscal 2026.
